departures: All fourteen markets qualified (300 or more decisive trades). The study ran on fourteen, not on a subset chosen after the run.

IN50: the proxy serves no candle after 12 Jul 2022, so its decisive window is 2016 to mid-2022 (1,415 trades), and its 2011-15 candles give no trade at the pre-registered session (fewer than 100): no replication figures. ES35: candles from 1 Dec 2016 only, no replication.

JP225, NL25 and CN50 start their replication later than their first candle (Apr 2010, Feb 2008, Sep 2011): before that the file has no candle at one of the cash-session boundaries (candle existence only; the cash-day rule of the pre-registration drops those days). The JP225 file starts in 2005 with candles outside Tokyo hours only.
The 'gap' drops are cash days whose next cash day was more than five calendar days later (long local holidays such as Lunar New Year, Easter, year end, or holes in the file), as pre-registered.

Financing is the frozen US-rate model for every market (said in the pre-registration); a non-US CFD is financed on its own currency's rate. Even with financing set to zero the pooled 2016-26 figure is gross minus spread only: +0.011R - 0.022R = about -0.011R a trade, still negative.
No figure was changed after the run; notes.json holds only the gate record, these lines and the reading.
reading: The gross overnight gain replicates on the pre-registered bar, weakly in 2016-26 and clearly before. Pooled over the fourteen index CFDs no overnight study used, the frozen close-to-open long made +0.011R a trade before any cost in 2016-26 (n 36,701, 130 months, month-sum t +2.10, Holm p 0.036) and +0.027R in 2005-15 (n 27,991, twelve markets, t +4.41). It is not a US-only effect: before costs every market but UK100 and CH20 was positive in 2016-26 and all twelve with a replication window were positive there (t +2.0 to +4.5). But two things limit what that means. First, in 2016-26 the pooled gross sits inside the duration-matched random-window placebo (rank 29 of 40; placebo +0.000 / +0.008 / +0.016R): holding these markets long for the same number of hours starting at a random time of day earned nearly as much, so most of the recent gross is the markets' own rise, not a night-specific drift (the month-sum t of +2.10 is above the placebo's 95th percentile of t, +1.84, which rests on a lower spread of monthly sums, not a higher mean). In 2005-15 the night did beat every placebo run (rank 40 of 40). Second, after the frozen cost model the result is a clear loss: -0.025R a trade (t -4.83), every market negative in 2016-26 (UK100 t -7.5, CH20 t -7.7), and still negative at zero financing (spread alone is about 0.022R a trade, twice the gross). The drift is about 0.01-0.03R a night at a one-ATR stop and a 0.03 % round-trip spread takes all of it on every market, as on US500 and NAS100. Net FAIL. Never call this an edge; it is not a council system and nothing live changed. A cheaper route (futures) would need its own pre-registration and, given the 2016-26 placebo, would first have to show the night beats a random hold of the same length.
